problem: Recurrent models compute positions sequentially, which prevents parallelization within training examples. Convolutional models compute positions in parallel, but the operations needed to relate two distant positions grow with distance (linearly for ConvS2S, logarithmically for ByteNet), making long-range dependencies harder to learn.
method: Transformer: encoder-decoder using only self-attention and multi-head attention (N=6 layers, h=8 heads), no recurrence or convolutions.
data: WMT 2014 English-to-German (~4.5M sentence pairs, BPE, 37,000-token shared vocabulary) and English-to-French (36M sentences, word-piece, 32,000-token vocabulary).
evaluation_setting: newstest2014; beam size 4, length penalty 0.6, checkpoint averaging (last 5 for base, last 20 for big models).
result: 28.4 BLEU (Transformer big, WMT 2014 English-to-German, trained 3.5 days on 8 P100 GPUs).
baseline_if_reported: ConvS2S Ensemble 26.36 BLEU; GNMT + RL Ensemble 26.30 BLEU.
limitation: Self-attention is slower than recurrent layers when sequence length n exceeds representation dimension d; restricting attention to a neighbourhood r raises maximum path length to O(n/r).
source_location: Method: Sec 1 p2; Sec 3.1-3.2 pp3-5. Result: Sec 6.1 p8, Table 2 p8 (big-model configuration: Table 3 p9). Limitation: Sec 4 pp6-7, Table 1 p6.

problem: Task-specific fine-tuning needs large labelled datasets, limits use on new tasks, can exploit spurious correlations and is far less sample-efficient than humans.
method: GPT-3: 175B-parameter autoregressive Transformer (96 layers, 96 heads, alternating dense and locally banded sparse attention), applied with no fine-tuning or gradient updates.
data: 300B tokens: filtered Common Crawl (60%), WebText2 (22%), Books1 (8%), Books2 (8%), Wikipedia (3%).
evaluation_setting: Over two dozen NLP benchmarks under zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting (K typically 10-100, 2,048-token context).
result: 71.2% (GPT-3 175B, few-shot K=64, TriviaQA closed-book, test server).
baseline_if_reported: T5-11B+SSM fine-tuned closed-book 60.5%; fine-tuned open-domain RAG 68.0%.
limitation: The authors say the left-to-right (autoregressive) design may hurt tasks that involve looking back and comparing two pieces of content; few-shot WiC is 49.4% (chance level) and some reading-comprehension tasks (e.g. QuAC, RACE) lag fine-tuned models. They state this as a likely cost of the design, not a proven cause.
source_location: Method: Sec 2.1 p8, Table 2.1 p8; Abstract p1. Result: Sec 3.2 p13, Table 3.3 p13; Fig 3.3 p14. Limitation: Sec 3.7 Table 3.8 pp19-20; Sec 5 p33.

problem: Pre-trained language models store knowledge implicitly in parameters, so memory is hard to expand or revise, provenance is hard to inspect, and hallucination is hard to prevent.
method: RAG: BART-large (~400M parameters) generator plus a Dense Passage Retriever over a dense Wikipedia index, trained end-to-end; RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token marginalize over retrieved documents.
data: Dec 2018 Wikipedia split into 21M 100-word chunks (FAISS MIPS); tasks: open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, CuratedTrec), MS-MARCO, Jeopardy question generation, FEVER.
evaluation_setting: Fine-tuned on input-output pairs; open-domain QA retrieves k in {5,10} documents in training and 15 (RAG-Token) or 50 (RAG-Sequence) at test time, Exact Match scoring.
result: 44.5 EM (RAG-Sequence, Natural Questions test set, 50 retrieved documents).
baseline_if_reported: T5-11B+SSM closed-book 36.6 EM; REALM 40.4 EM; DPR 41.5 EM.
limitation: Retrieval collapse in preliminary story-generation experiments: the retriever returns the same documents regardless of input and the generator ignores them.
source_location: Method: Sec 1 p2; Sec 2.1-2.3 p3. Result: Sec 4.1 p6, Table 1 p6; Appendix A p17. Limitation: Appendix H p19.

problem: Reasoning-only prompting hallucinates and propagates errors; action-only agents lack working memory and goal decomposition.
method: ReAct: prompt a frozen LLM to interleave free-form thoughts with environment actions so reasoning guides actions and observations update reasoning.
data: HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld (134 unseen games, 6 task types), WebShop (1.18M products, 500 test instructions).
evaluation_setting: Frozen PaLM-540B prompted with 1-6 few-shot human trajectories, greedy decoding, no gradient updates.
result: 71% (ReAct, PaLM-540B, ALFWorld, best of 6 trials; average of 6 trials 57%).
baseline_if_reported: BUTLER imitation learning 37% (best of 8); Act-only prompting 45% (best of 6).
limitation: Interleaving thoughts and actions reduces reasoning flexibility: in the authors' manual analysis of sampled HotpotQA failures, reasoning errors were 47% of ReAct failures vs 16% of CoT failures (Table 2), including repetitive loops. These are shares of sampled failures, not overall error rates.
source_location: Method: Sec 1 p2; Sec 2 pp2-3. Result: Sec 4 p8, Table 3 p8. Limitation: Sec 3.3 pp5-6, Table 2 p6.

problem: LLMs often fail complex generation requirements on the first try, and existing refinement methods need supervised data, human annotation or external reward models.
method: SELF-REFINE: one frozen LLM generates an output, writes multi-aspect feedback on it, and refines it iteratively (up to 4 iterations; maximum k=3 for dialogue response generation) using few-shot prompts.
data: 7 tasks: dialogue response (FED: 372 conversations; 342 test instances used for automatic evaluation and 100 instances evaluated by humans), code optimization (PIE), code readability (CodeNet), math (GSM-8k), sentiment reversal (Yelp), acronym generation, constrained generation (CommonGen-Hard).
evaluation_setting: GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, GPT-4 and Codex, up to 4 iterations (maximum k=3 for dialogue), temperature 0.7; refined output compared with the model's initial output.
metric: Preference score (%); judge uncertain because sources conflict (Sec 3.2 p5 mentions GPT-4 as a proxy for human preference; Appendix M p33 says text-davinci-003 was the automatic judge)
result: 74.6% preference for GPT-4 + SELF-REFINE (k=3) vs 25.4% for base GPT-4 on FED dialogue response generation (+49.2 points); judge uncertain.
limitation: Base model must already follow few-shot instructions well enough to give structured feedback; weaker models such as Vicuna-13B fail or hallucinate.
source_location: Method: Sec 1 p1; Sec 2 pp2-3; Sec 3.1 p4. Result: Sec 3.3 p5, Table 1 p5; Appendix M.2 p32; Appendix M p33. Data: Table 4 p14. Limitation: Sec 4 pp7-8; Sec 6 p9.
